acceptance.given: The Toolchain evaluator is run with identity or execution facts that are unknown, missing, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable.

oracle.expected: The evaluation records a rejected or explicitly non-success outcome and does not emit an accepted success status.
forbidden: An ambiguous identity or execution fact is treated as verified.
Success is reported or accepted despite unresolved identity or execution ambiguity.
oracle.observable: A deterministic validator result containing the ambiguity classification and a non-success verdict.

acceptance.when: During the identity/execution-fact success gate evaluation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the existing semantic-gate validator against a case with an ambiguous or unverifiable identity/execution fact; it must fail if the result is accepted as success.

affected_subjects: identity and execution fact success gate
slice_hint.behavior_change: Classify unknown, missing, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable identity/execution facts as non-success before success determination.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep the existing evaluator result schema and reject only unresolved identity or execution facts; no persistent-state migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: Ambiguous facts produce a rejected or non-success verdict; verified facts retain the existing success flow.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Terminal only when every ambiguous identity or execution input yields deterministic non-success and none yields accepted success.

acceptance.given: The SM-1 witness-completeness evaluation is run over the frozen atomic-obligation inventory and its Exact Cover data.

oracle.expected: The coverage report proves 100% bidirectional required-witness coverage, with zero uncovered obligations and zero orphan witnesses.
forbidden: Any atomic obligation lacks a required witness.
oracle.observable: A machine-readable Exact Cover and witness report listing every atomic obligation with required witnesses and reporting zero orphans.

acceptance.when: When the SM-1 witness-completeness report is generated and validated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the Exact Cover/witness validator with one atomic obligation missing its required witness; validation must fail and identify the uncovered obligation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate bidirectional witness coverage for every atomic obligation and reject incomplete or orphaned witness mappings.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing Exact Cover artifact schema while enforcing required-witness completeness and orphan detection.

slice_hint.state_transition: Inventory and witness declarations produce a reconciled 100% coverage report or deterministic failure.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Terminal only when every inventory obligation has all required witnesses, every witness references an inventory obligation, and the report states zero orphans.

acceptance.given: The SM-2 adversarial evaluation runs a case whose Consumer is intentionally skipped while other case inputs remain valid.

oracle.expected: The case terminates with a rejected-success or non-success verdict, and the report identifies the skipped Consumer as the cause.
forbidden: Success is accepted for a skipped-Consumer case.
The evaluator silently omits the skipped Consumer from coverage or verdict computation.
oracle.observable: A deterministic case result containing skipped-Consumer evidence and a rejected-success verdict.

acceptance.when: When the SM-2 skipped-Consumer adversarial case is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the SM-2 skipped-Consumer case through the semantic-verdict validator; it must fail if the case is reported successful.

affected_subjects: success determination for skipped Consumer cases
slice_hint.behavior_change: Treat skipped Consumers as explicit negative evidence that forces a rejected-success or non-success verdict.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain existing case-result fields and validate skipped-Consumer status without changing route compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: Skipped Consumer detected -> rejected-success or non-success terminal verdict.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Terminal only when every skipped-Consumer case is explicitly rejected or non-success and no skipped case can produce accepted success.

acceptance.given: An aggregate execution is started with its applicable time and output bounds configured.

oracle.expected: Every aggregate records terminal completion within its applicable bound; timeout, budget exhaustion, or unbounded activity yields deterministic unsuccessful status.
forbidden: An aggregate exceeds its time bound.
An aggregate remains active without a bounded terminal outcome.
Budget exhaustion is reported as success.
oracle.observable: Per-aggregate execution evidence containing start/end timestamps, configured bound, terminal status, and elapsed time at or below the bound.

acceptance.when: For each aggregate execution, after its terminal result and timing evidence are captured.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the aggregate timeout harness with a deliberately over-budget aggregate; validation must observe timeout or budget exhaustion and reject success.

affected_subjects: aggregate execution time/output bounds and terminal state
slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce bounded aggregate execution with deterministic terminal evidence and unsuccessful status on timeout or budget exhaustion.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve command and result interfaces while enforcing bounds through existing process execution and semantic-gate evidence fields.

slice_hint.state_transition: Aggregate starts -> bounded execution -> terminal success or timeout/budget-exhaustion non-success.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Terminal only when elapsed time is recorded for each aggregate, is at or below its bound for success, and timeout or budget exhaustion is terminal non-success.
